subject: Executive and Legislative Charter Provisions
overview: The subcommittee reviewed proposed draft provisions for Articles 2 and 3 of the Medford City Charter, covering appointments, removals, vacancies, and oversight powers. Members aligned on proposing 30-day confirmation timelines and access-to-information mechanisms while identifying several areas for further research and consultation with the Collins Center.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The subcommittee approved the previous meeting's minutes.

items.title: Review of Multi-Member Body Appointment Procedures
items.summary: The committee agreed to propose a 30-day window for City Council to veto mayoral board appointments or approve them earlier by a two-thirds vote, while deciding against charter mandates for applicant reply letters.

items.title: Creation of Boards and Advisory Committees
items.summary: Members agreed to request a primer from the Collins Center regarding how permanent and ad hoc committees are established across Massachusetts municipalities.

items.title: Department Head Appointments and Removals
items.summary: The subcommittee supported applying the same 30-day confirmation procedure to department heads but favored leaving department head removal power solely to the mayor without City Council involvement.

items.title: City Clerk and Council Staff
items.summary: Members agreed to maintain City Council appointment of the city clerk, allow for an optional clerk of the council position, and permit council staffing subject to appropriation.

items.title: City Auditor
items.summary: The committee debated whether to include a council-appointed city auditor versus independent periodic audits, assigning Moreshi to research Medford's current practices.

items.title: City Council and Mayoral Vacancies
items.summary: The subcommittee agreed that council vacancies should continue going to the next highest vote-getter with council appointment as a backstop, and discussed filling mayoral vacancies via special election within 120 days or by an acting mayor.

items.title: Council Oversight and Access to Information
items.summary: Members favored charter language modeled on Melrose allowing the City Council to compel the attendance of the mayor, employees, and board chairs with 10 days' notice, while rejecting subpoena powers for private citizens.

items.title: Scheduling and Next Steps
items.summary: The subcommittee scheduled its next meeting for November 30, 2023, to complete the draft review before presenting to the full committee.
